newsitem.title: USA: Tabloid newspaper to fight Eddie Murphy's lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Tabloid newspaper to fight Eddie Murphy's lawsuit.

text.p: A tabloid newspaper said on Thursday it will fight a lawsuit brought against it by comedian Eddie Murphy alleging it printed lies about his sexual tastes.

The National Enquirer printed the article after Murphy was stopped by undercover police with a transsexual prostitute in his vehicle. The Enquirer said in a statement it stood by its story and would not "tolerate this legal attack."
"Mr. Murphy is attempting to rehabilitate himself at our expense. We intend to prove our case in open court," the statement added.

Murphy filed two lawsuits in Los Angeles Superior Cour on Wednesday, seeking $5 million in general damages and unspecified punitive damages each from the National Enquirer and the Globe tabloid paper for slander, libel and invasion of privacy.
A third lawsuit by Murphy seeks at least $1 million for the same reasons from Ioane Seiuli, a relative of the prostitute who was in Murphy's car on the morning of May 2.
Atisone Seiuli was arrested by sheriff's deputies on an outstanding prostitution warrant in the incident on Santa Monica Boulevard in West Hollywood. Murphy, 36, was not charged with any offence.

After the incident, Murphy said in interviews and through his publicist that he had been giving Seiuli a ride home and that he was a "Good Samaritan" who often helped out the homeless and prostitutes.

Murphy, described in the lawsuits as "an internationally renowned comedian and actor," alleged the tabloids printed articles knowing they were false or without reasonable grounds for believing they were true.
The tabloids printed interviews with transvestite prostitutes suggesting Murphy had a "secret sex life" and a "sick obsession."
His lawsuit against Ioane Seiuli, whose sex is not specified, relates to comments Seiuli made to the New York Post.

The Enquirer's statement said television personality Geraldo Rivera taped a show on Wednesday for later airing in which he interviewed a number of transsexuals who claimed to have had sex with Murphy. The transsexuals were given polygraph tests on the show that indicated they were telling the truth, the tabloid said.
In addition, the Enquirer said, radio personality Howard Stern recently had a transsexual on his show who described a sexual encounter with Murphy.
Murphy and his publicist could not be reached to comment on the Enquirer's statement. A spokesman for the Globe was not available. Ioane Seiuli was also unavailable to comment.
